school: 文艺复兴盛期雕塑家/画家（大卫像、西斯廷天顶画、最后的审判）/建筑师（圣彼得大教堂穹顶）/诗人
historical_significance: 米开朗基罗·博那罗蒂（1475-1564），生于托斯卡纳卡普雷塞，是文艺复兴盛期最伟大的雕塑家，与达芬奇、拉斐尔并称文艺复兴三杰。26岁时接手被两位雕塑家放弃、在主教座堂工坊院中曝晒二十余年的大理石废料，雕刻出5.17米的《大卫》，成为佛罗伦萨自由的象征。1508-1512年独自仰卧脚手架四年，完成西斯廷礼拜堂天顶画五百余平方米、三百余人物（《创世纪》系列）；1536-1541年又以《最后的审判》覆盖其祭坛墙。晚年主持圣彼得大教堂穹顶设计，并创作大量诗歌。他自视为雕塑家而非画家，信奉'雕像本在石中，我只是凿去多余'——从材料内部看见形式、以减法释放形式，把人体的扭曲与张力（terribilità）推到极限。瓦萨里在《名人传》中把他作为艺术史第一个被神化的在世艺术家。1564年逝于罗马。
historical_significance_en: Michelangelo Buonarroti (1475-1564), born in Caprese, Tuscany, is the supreme sculptor of the High Renaissance, ranked with Leonardo and Raphael. At 26 he took a colossal block of Carrara marble abandoned by two sculptors and weathering in the cathedral workshop yard for over two decades, and carved the 5.17-metre David, symbol of Florentine liberty. From 1508-1512, lying on his back on scaffolding for four years, he alone painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling—over 500 square metres, 300+ figures (the Genesis cycle); from 1536-1541 he covered its altar wall with The Last Judgment. In old age he directed the dome of St Peter's Basilica and wrote abundant poetry. He regarded himself as a sculptor, not a painter, believing the statue already lives within the stone and he merely carves away the excess—seeing form inside matter and releasing it by subtraction, pushing the torsion and terribilità of the human figure to its limit. Vasari canonized him in the Lives as the first living artist deified by art history. He died in Rome in 1564.
description_zh: 减法创造者的思维原型：在废弃材料中看见被囚禁的形式，用预见的整体约束每一步减法，以身体劳动为认识工具，在限制（不完美石料、仰视曲面、生前未竟）中完成伟大的作品。
description_en: The prototype of the subtractive creator: see the imprisoned form inside discarded matter, let a foreseen whole govern every cut of subtraction, use bodily labour as an instrument of knowledge, and achieve greatness within constraints—flawed stone, curved surfaces seen from below, works left unfinished.
